content.text:
I released **[v0.36.2](https://github.com/cv/pit/releases/tag/v0.36.2)**, following `docs/releasing.md`. It ships the pi-durable image support from #365 (#366).

- **Release PR:** #367 bumps `package.json` and `package-lock.json` to 0.36.2, moves the Unreleased changelog entries under `## [0.36.2] - 2026-11-13` and points the README's pinned install line at `v0.36.2`. Before it went up, `delivery.validate` passed (static checks, tests, coverage and the package check), `npm audit` found 0 vulnerabilities, and `npm pack --dry-run` showed 183 files at 319.4 kB. Its checks passed and I rebase-merged it.
- **Tag:** CI passed on the merged `main` commit (`61457eb`) on Node 22, 24 and 26. I then pushed the annotated tag `v0.36.2` on that commit.
- **Published release:** the Release workflow succeeded. `release.verifyPublished` confirmed the release points at `61457eb` and has no assets. A fresh clone of the tag installed its runtime dependencies at version 0.36.2, and a test script in the sandbox returned `2`.

**Still to do:** I haven't run the interactive smoke test on the installed tag (install it in Pi, `/reload`, then try the checklist in the guide). It matters for this release because #366 also refactored the shared image code that `workspace.viewImage` uses on regular Pi. If you want to check that by hand, view an image on Pi once.

**Version number:** this release adds a feature (the `images` option), which would normally mean a minor version. I made it a patch release as you asked; Pit is still on 0.x.
